# Seirḗn: the stories first, then the spelling

Before the spelling, the story. **Seirḗn** earns its restoration the old way — through what was actually told.

## The Stories That Carry the Name

**The Passage of the Mast.** Kirkē warns Odysseus before he sails: the Seirḗnes “enchant all who come near,” and their island, Anthemoessa — the “flowery” — is heaped with “bones of dead men, in great heaps, and round them the flesh is rotting” (Od.  12. 39–46).

**Out-Sung by Orpheus.** Apollonius Rhodius sends the Argo down the same strait a generation before Odysseus, and the solution is not wax but art.  As the Sirens' cry drifts over the water, “sweetly singing the homes of the blessed,” Orpheus takes up his lyre and strikes “a chord of blazing music...  a song so loud that the singing of the Sirens was drowned in it” (Arg.

**The Wings That Searched.** The later tradition gives the Seirḗnes their wings as an instrument of grief.  Euripides has Helen invoke the “winged maidens, servants of the daughter of Demeter” — the Seirḗnes as mourners in Persephonē's retinue (Hel.  167–178).

## And Here Is What the Spelling Preserves

Against those stories, the attestation: **Σειρήν**, as Homer, Odyssey 12.39–200 (Circe's warning; the passage; the Sirens' promise of knowledge) and Apollonius Rhodius, Argonautica 4.885–921 (Orpheus' counter-song; Butēs) preserve it. The name means "Binder, entangler".


## At a Glance

- **Restored name:** Seirḗn
- **ASCII form:** seiren
- **Meaning:** "Binder, entangler"
- **Domain of influence:** Enchanting Singer
- **Pantheon:** Greek
- **Classification:** Tier 1
- **Original script:** Σειρήν
- **Series:** The Restoration Files, No. 428 of 546

## The Name Travels

Late antiquity moralized her: Christian writers made the Sirens the seductions of the world, the mast the cross.  The Middle Ages merged her with the fish-tailed northern mermaid — the bird-maiden of Greece becoming the siren of romance — and French gave the world sirène, which is why modern alarm sirens and mermaids share a word.

## The Address It Earned

The temple of **Seirḗn** stands at [/seiren/](/seiren/) — [lore](/seiren/lore/), [scholars](/seiren/scholars/), [patterns](/seiren/patterns/) — because a name carrying this much story deserves more than a parking page. Tier-1 is not a compliment; it is a measurement. This restoration keeps something the ASCII form provably loses, and the measurement is repeatable.

## The Sources Are Open

The myths above are retold from the temple's record; the primary voices are in the [Sacred Texts](/texts/): [Theogony](/texts/theogony/), [Homeric Hymns](/texts/homeric-hymns/), and [Works and Days](/texts/works-and-days/). Nothing in this file outranks them.
